There are two directions, and you can use both:
Your agent reaches you. Claude Code, OpenClaw, n8n or a script messages your phone, waits for your reply, or calls you. A voice AI talks to you for the agent and hands it the transcript. Use the MCP server (or its HTTP version ), the CLI or the relay's REST API.
You reach your agents by phone. On a call (one the agent placed, or one you made with "Call agent" in the app), the voice AI can ask your agents for help. Each agent in agents.yaml is a tool for it, through consult_agent , and so are your MCP servers.
agentring mcp is an MCP server over stdio. Add it to any MCP client:
The second form is the usual mcpServers config that most clients read. It uses the daemon's config ( agentring init ), so run agentring init and agentring pair first. Other harnesses: see recipes .
agentring mcp --agent-name "Claude Code" sets the caller name the phone shows (useful when several agents share one relay), and --device dev_… (repeatable) rings only those phones instead of every paired one.
call blocks until the call ends, and get_replies up to wait_s : raise the client's MCP tool timeout if it has a short one (Codex: 60 s, opencode: 30 s).
context is everything the voice AI knows about the agent's work: put in it what to tell you, what to ask and what not to decide. If ~/.agentring/agents.yaml exists, the voice AI on these calls can also consult your agents.
The server is a small JSON-RPC loop with no MCP SDK and no extra dependencies (see architecture ). For an MCP URL instead of a local command, see Remote MCP (HTTP) . HTTP-only clients such as n8n can also use the REST API (below).
agentring mcp-http serves the same four tools over MCP Streamable HTTP at /mcp , for many users at once. Each user's agent sends its relay API key as a bearer token, so nothing about the user is configured on the server, and the agent's computer needs no daemon:
Run it next to your relay (self-hosted: every key is checked against that one relay with GET /v1/status ):
Auth. No key, or one the relay (or hub) doesn't know: 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer . A working key is remembered for 5 minutes (by its hash; keys are never logged).
Protocol. POST /mcp takes JSON-RPC ( initialize , ping , tools/list , tools/call , notifications, notifications/cancelled ; batches too). initialize returns an Mcp-Session-Id ; send it back on later requests (an unknown or expired one gets 404: initialize again). Requests without a session id also work. DELETE /mcp ends the session and cancels its running requests; GET /mcp is 405 (the server sends nothing unprompted). GET /healthz is the health check.
Long calls. Quick requests get application/json . call , and get_replies with wait_s , get a text/event-stream (if the client accepts it) with a keep-alive comment every 15 s until the result, so proxies don't cut the request. Raise the proxy's read timeout anyway if it is shorter than a call. If the client hangs up, a waiting get_replies stops; a phone call goes on until it ends.
Voice. call runs the voice AI on this server, with the provider and key from its environment ( AGENTRING_VOICE_PROVIDER , GEMINI_API_KEY , …) as for agentring call --ai . agents.yaml is not used: the server never runs commands for its users.
State. Which replies get_replies already returned is kept per tenant (hub tenant id, or the relay id in self-hosted mode) in {data dir}/tenants/{id}.db , the same mirror the local daemon keeps, so every session of one user sees each reply once, also after a restart.
With Docker, the daemon image ( daemon/Dockerfile , entrypoint agentring ) runs it; for example as a service in deploy/docker-compose.yml , routed at /mcp by the proxy:
~/.agentring/agents.yaml (or --agents PATH ) lists what the voice AI may use during a call:
command is an argv list, never a shell string (a string is rejected). The task comes from a voice model, so it is only ever one argument: {task} is replaced inside the argument that contains it, and if no argument has it, the task goes to stdin. The agent's stdout is the answer. A non-zero exit is an error, with the end of stderr.
Don't let the task be read as an option: put -- before {task} , or text before it in the same argument ( "Task: {task}" ).
The agent runs with your environment plus env and AGENTRING_CALL_ID , in cwd . The call id lets an agent keep one session per call (see OpenClaw ).
description matters : the voice AI picks the agent by it.
Over the phone, expose only what the caller should be able to do: use allowlists, and agents whose permissions you'd accept from someone holding your phone. The phone is paired to your relay, but the voice AI acts on what it hears.
Check the file and try an agent without a call:
consult_agent(agent, task) waits up to 20 s. If the agent answers in that time, the voice AI gets the answer right away. If not, it hears that the agent is working on it, tells you, and the call carries on. When the answer arrives, the voice AI gets it as a note and tells you. If the call has already ended, the answer is sent to your phone as a message. Each agent works on one task at a time; a second request for a busy agent is refused, so the model asks again later.
From Python, Consultations(agents, answer_within_s=…, prompts=ConsultPrompts(…)) builds the tool ( .tool() ) for a VoiceAgent . Any tool of your own can do the same "answer later" trick: current_session() returns the call, and session.notify(text, respond=True) speaks up when you are done.
agentring doesn't care which harness you use: anything that speaks MCP can reach you, and anything you can run as a command can be consulted from a call.
Add skills/agentring where the harness reads skills, so the agent knows when to message and when to call.
You consult your agent from a call ( agents.yaml )
Keep only the ones you use, and check each with agentring agents ask "…" . They start read-only or with the harness's own approval rules. Widen them on purpose, knowing the voice AI acts on what it hears:
Claude Code : plan can look but not change anything. To let it act, use --permission-mode acceptEdits with a narrow --allowedTools list.
Codex : --sandbox workspace-write lets it edit files under cwd . Add --skip-git-repo-check if cwd is not a git repo.
opencode : uses its permission config; don't add --auto (approves everything). With opencode serve running, --attach http://localhost:4096 skips the start-up cost.
Hermes : -z prints only the final answer. Don't add --yolo for the phone.
openclaw agent runs one turn through your running gateway. The sh -c script is fixed text: the task arrives as $1 and is never parsed by the shell. The call id gives each call its own OpenClaw session, so a second question on the same call keeps the context of the first.
For an agent that only runs as a server (an OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as the OpenClaw gateway's or Hermes' API server, a webhook, your own service), point command at a small script that reads the task on stdin and prints the answer:
Every action is one HTTPS request to your relay with the daemon's ak_… API key ( agentring status --json prints the relay URL; the key is in ~/.agentring/.env ). See protocol/relay.openapi.yaml :
Replies come from GET /v1/messages?after= , or live over the WebSocket. A call over plain REST only rings the phone: the voice needs a worker in the room, which is the daemon ( agentring call --ai , or the call MCP tool). See examples/ for an n8n workflow.
